label: lem:zero_deriv_constant
title: Zero derivative implies constant
statement: Let $G : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ be continuous on $[a,b]$ and differentiable on $(a,b)$ with $G'(x) = 0$ for all $x \in (a,b)$. Then $G$ is constant on $[a,b]$. In Mathlib this is \texttt{is\_const\_of\_deriv\_eq\_zero}.
proof: By the Mean Value Theorem (Lemma~\ref{lem:mean_value_theorem}), for any $x, y \in [a,b]$ with $x < y$, there exists $c \in (x,y)$ such that $G(y) - G(x) = G'(c)(y-x) = 0$.
